title: Your call, defended
kicker: World 7 · Decide Where It Matters · Level 3

job.text:
A new workflow you haven't seen: a hospital discharge-instructions assistant. Tier every step by the cost of being wrong, hard-gate the one step that must be exact, and name the single riskiest step.

The real ask here is free text — "for each step, tell me the cost of being wrong and bucket it (hard gate / heuristic / human); name the riskiest step and defend it in one sentence." For now you build that ask from the chips below; your pass is decided by the hidden expert key, never by the AI reading your words. The one-sentence defense is stored for a human to read and does not gate the result.

rows: Summarize the diagnosis in plain words
List warning signs to watch for
Decide whether to escalate to a nurse

naivePrompt: Treat it like the billing one.
basePrompt: Treat it like the billing one.

text.plain: Hard-gate the dosage calculation — it has one right answer and the highest cost of being wrong, so a tool must compute it.
text.tech: Mark step 1 (dosage) gate: hard; the number is computed by a tool, not estimated, even though a human also reviews it.

moves.label: Name the dosage as the riskiest step

text.plain: Flag the dosage as the single riskiest step — a dosage error can harm a patient.
text.tech: Set riskiest = step 1 (dosage); attach the one-sentence defense (stored for human review).

text.plain: Send the escalate-to-a-nurse decision to a human — it's a judgment call about patient care.
text.tech: Mark step 6 (escalate) gate: human; route to a clinician.

text.plain: Hard-gate the next-appointment lookup — a date lookup has one right value.
text.tech: Mark step 4 (next appointment) gate: hard; the date comes from a lookup, not a guess.

text.plain: Copy the tiers from the billing workflow — but a different domain has different risks.
text.tech: Reuse the billing tiering verbatim — ignoring that a dosage error harms a patient.

text.plain: Hard-gate the warning-signs list — but a list of symptoms has no single exact right answer to gate against.
text.tech: Mark step 5 (warning signs) gate: hard — but there is no one exact list to gate.

rules.claim: The billing tiers were copied over — and the dosage ended up tiered like a payment plan.
rules.feedback: Different workflow, different risks. "Treat it like billing" misses that a dosage error harms a patient. Tier for this job.

output.source: the billing tiers reused on a clinical workflow

rules.claim: Dosage hard-gated and named riskiest — but you also hard-gated the warning-signs list.
rules.feedback: You found the moves that do the work, but you also hard-gated the warning-signs list. A list of symptoms has no single exact answer to gate against, so that gate catches nothing — hard-gating the dosage and naming it the riskiest step are what matter. Take it out so you know exactly which call carried the judgment.
rules.lesson: Gate the exact high-cost step; a hard gate on an open-ended list just rides along — drop it.

output.source: the right calls, plus a wasteful gate on an open-ended list

rules.claim: Dosage → hard gate and named the riskiest step; the defense is stored for a nurse to read.
rules.feedback: Defended and correct. You hard-gated the dosage, flagged it as the riskiest, and said why in one line. That's the judgment the whole ladder was building to.
rules.lesson: On a new domain, find the exact high-cost step and gate it hard.

output.source: the hidden expert key for this domain

rules.claim: The dosage wasn't hard-gated — it was left to be estimated or named something other than the riskiest step.
rules.feedback: The dosage needs a hard gate. It has one right answer and the highest cost of being wrong — a human reviews it, but the number itself must be computed by a tool, not estimated. And it is the step to name as riskiest.
rules.lesson: The highest-cost exact step is always hard-gated.

hints.nudge: In THIS workflow, which single step would do the most harm if wrong?
hints.gap: Narrow to the two clinical steps — one of them is a calculation.
hints.moves: Hard-gate the dosage calculation and name it the riskiest step. Leave the greeting, the diagnosis summary and the warning-signs list on heuristic; the escalate decision goes to a human.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: Reuse the billing tiers → the dosage goes ungated.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: Tier for this domain, hard-gate the dosage, name and defend the riskiest step.

template.plain: New workflow. For each step, tell me the cost of being wrong and bucket it: must be exact (tool-gated) / best-effort / human decides. Name the single riskiest step and defend it in one sentence.
template.tech: New workflow. For each step annotate gate: hard | heuristic | human from cost-of-wrong, not from what's easy. Hard-gate every step with a single correct value; name the riskiest step and store a one-line defense for human review.

notes: ChatGPT: make it reason from cost-of-wrong, not from what's easy to automate.
Copilot in Excel: the exact, high-cost steps are the ones you turn into checked formulas.
A chat AI that can't run code: you own the high-stakes calls; use its tiering as input, not the decision — and never accept "the dosage looks right" without a tool and a person on it.
